title: Neural Efficiency and Attentional Instability in Gaming Disorder: A Task-Based Occipital EEG and Machine Learning Study.
summary: Five machine-learning classifiers classified gaming-disorder EEG from occipital task recordings in 15 affected and 15 control participants using subject-independent leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
ai_technology: Five machine-learning classifiers classified gaming-disorder EEG from occipital task recordings in 15 affected and 15 control participants using subject-independent leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.

evidence.tested: Performance was evaluated across five LOSO folds with held-out subjects; the 30-person sample and task-specific EEG design limit diagnostic inference.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed source does not establish prospective benefit, broad external validity, or replication beyond the reported study.
